descriptor: Operating company · reported in BRL · quoted in USD

kpis.label: Net Income (continuing ops)
kpis.note: Excludes discontinued Linx; the post-divestment bottom line

charts.title: Net Income: Total vs Continuing Operations
charts.annotation: Continuing-ops net income excludes the divested Linx software business and 2026 one-off disposal effects; it only differs from total net income from FY2023 onward, before which StoneCo did not separately report it.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For StoneCo Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For StoneCo Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date. Total debt here is funding for the merchant-credit book; it sits alongside a growing retail deposit base from Conta Stone (StoneCo's digital banking product), which the filings disclose separately and which grew from R$4.0bn (FY2022) to R$11.1bn (FY2025) — an increasingly important low-cost funding source for the credit business that is not in this chart's borrowings figure.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Retail deposit growth as a cheaper substitute for wholesale/institutional funding of the credit book
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For StoneCo Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For StoneCo Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For StoneCo Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For StoneCo Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Net income (total) includes discontinued operations; net income (continuing ops) excludes the Linx software business StoneCo sold to TOTVS in 2026 and is the cleaner read of the ongoing payments-banking-credit business.

For StoneCo Ltd.: FY2022 and FY2024 total net income swung negative on one-off items (Linx impairments, the FY2026 disposal charge); continuing-ops net income is only reported from FY2023, so the two lines are identical before then and diverge afterward — that divergence IS the comparability break, not a data error.

What to watch:

  • Whether swings are one-off (disposal, impairment) or operating
  • Continuing-ops net income as the base for forward comparisons, not the lumpier total

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue here is continuing operations: transaction/subscription revenue from merchant acquiring (MDR on card and Pix TPV) plus financial income — receivables-prepayment (anticipation), credit and float on client balances — which management discloses running roughly 71-74% of total revenue, making it the dominant line, not a footnote to MDR.

For StoneCo Ltd.: the pre-2026 "as reported" total also included the now-divested Linx software business (R$12.1bn FY2023, R$13.3bn FY2024 as-reported vs R$10.8bn/R$12.0bn continuing-ops shown here) — a ~11% comparability break, not an organic decline, when comparing to filings published before the TOTVS sale closed. Financial income is itself interest-rate sensitive: it scales with Brazil's Selic/CDI rate as much as with payment volume.

What to watch:

  • Financial income growth vs. core MDR/transaction growth — a widening gap means the business is increasingly a credit/float spread, not a payments-take-rate story
  • Selic/CDI direction, which drives financial income independent of volume
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For StoneCo Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
